title: AI-ECG detects high-risk echocardiographic features in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
summary: A deep learning AI-ECG trained on 2,591 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients to predict any of four high-risk echocardiographic features (outflow tract obstruction, massive hypertrophy, systolic dysfunction, apical aneurysm) reached AUROC 0.81 (95% CI 0.76-0.86) in testing and 0.80 (95% CI 0.72-0.87) in a second-hospital external set of 171. The study is retrospective with a small external cohort; the abstract also describes monitoring feature changes over follow-up.
ai_technology: Deep learning AI-ECG model predicting the presence of high-risk echocardiographic features
organization: First Hospital of China Medical University

evidence.tested: Retrospective internal test and external validation at a second hospital (n=171).
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance, longitudinal monitoring accuracy and clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Screens ECGs for features otherwise needing echocardiography.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
